newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe Standard Chartered hikes lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe Standard Chartered hikes lending rate.

text.p: One of Zimbabwe's leading commercial banks, Standard Chartered, on Wednesday hiked its minimum lending rate by two percentage points to 27.5 percent points following a similar move last week by the central Reserve Bank.
The central bank announced on Friday it was increasing its rediscount rate -- the rate at which it lends to banks -- to 25.5 percent from 23.5 in a bid to combat inflationary pressures.
In the year to April, annual inflation rose to a 10-month high of 22.4 percent from 19.9 percent in March, and there are fears that this year's average will surpass last year's 21.7 percent.

In February Standard Chartered, again tracking the central bank, revised its lending rate 3.5 percent downwards on the back of predictions inflation would stay in a 16-18 percent band in the fourth quarter of the year.
But a spate of price hikes saw inflation jump to 19 percent in February from 15.8 percent in January.
